AI Impact on the Global Job Market: Risk, Salary & Skills Trend Analysis (2015–2035)

A comprehensive trend analysis examining how AI automation risk, salary dynamics, skill demand, and job survival prospects are evolving across roles, countries, and experience levels from 2015 to 2035.

Dataset: 12,343 recordsYears: 2015–2035Historical: 2015–2024Projected: 2025–2035Countries: 6Roles: 10

Executive Overview

Equip executive leadership and workforce strategists with data-driven insights into which job categories face the highest automation risk, how salaries and job openings are shifting over time, and which skills and education profiles offer the strongest future-proofing — enabling informed decisions on talent investment, reskilling programs, and strategic workforce planning.

Most critical takeaways
  • Across 12,343 records spanning 2015–2035, average AI risk increased from 0.30 to 0.51, a +0.21-point movement.
  • Median salary increased from $24,247 to $36,763 (+51.6%), while total annual job openings increased by +5.8%.
  • Job survival rate decreased from 91.1% to 83.7%; projected-period survival averages 87.7% versus 90.5% historically.
  • Business Analyst has the highest average AI risk (0.75); AI Researcher has the lowest (0.15). The highest-risk country is India (0.40).
  • Salary and automation risk show a record-level correlation of -0.24 and a job-title-level correlation of -0.81, indicating whether pay is aligned with exposure rather than assuming risk always lowers compensation.

Data integrity note: all metrics are computed from /app/benchmark/data.csv. Years 2025–2035 are treated as projected values per the source brief, not observed history.

AI Automation Risk Landscape

Automation exposure is measured by ai_risk_score and the pre-computed ai_risk_category. Across all records, the average AI risk score is 0.40; category shares are Low Risk 32.7%, Medium Risk 48.7%, and High Risk 18.6%.

The year trend moves from 0.30 in 2015 to 0.51 in 2035. Role-level exposure is concentrated at the top: Business Analyst leads at 0.75, while AI Researcher is lowest at 0.15. Country averages range from 0.39 in UK to 0.40 in India. Experience-level averages are Entry 0.40, Mid 0.40, and Senior 0.39.

Salary Trends & Segmentation

Median salary across the full dataset is $31,573. The annual median increased from $24,247 in 2015 to $36,763 in 2035, a +51.6% change. Salary bucket shares are Low 5.2%, Medium 17.0%, and High 77.7%.

Salary × automation risk insight: Across records, salary and AI risk have a correlation of -0.24; aggregated by job title, the relationship is -0.81. Median salary by AI risk category is $34,105 for Low Risk, $34,710 for Medium Risk, and $21,683 for High Risk. This indicates the dataset does not support a blanket assumption that higher automation risk always means lower compensation; workforce strategy should separate exposure from market value.

Skills Demand & Future-Proofing

Average skill demand across all records is 79.5. The annual average increased from 78.9 in 2015 to 80.2 in 2035. The highest average-demand skill is Java (79.9), and the fastest 2015–2035 growth is Java (+3.9 points).

Future-proofing differs by skill portfolio. Among skills, survival rates range from 43.0% to 100.0%, while average AI risk ranges from 0.15 to 0.75. Skills with both high demand and high survival should be prioritized for reskilling pathways.

Job Survival & Market Outlook

Job survival is calculated as the share of records with job_survival_class >= 1. Overall survival rate is 89.0%; class shares are At-risk 11.0%, Moderate survival 47.0%, and High survival 42.0%. From 2015 to 2035, the survival rate moved from 91.1% to 83.7%.

Total annual job openings increased from 14,024,622 in 2015 to 14,838,117 in 2035. The strongest openings expansion is Product Manager (+546,788), while the weakest movement is DevOps Engineer (-437,347).

Strategic Recommendations

Each recommendation is tied directly to measured trends in risk, salary, skill demand, survival classification, or openings growth.

Prioritize role-specific automation mitigationFocus governance, redesign, and augmentation plans first on Business Analyst, Data Analyst, and Software Engineer, the three roles with the highest average AI risk scores (0.75, 0.65, and 0.45).
Fund reskilling around rising skillsAllocate reskilling capacity toward Java, Python, and AWS, which post the largest 2015–2035 demand-score gains (+3.9, +3.0, and +2.7 points).
Use compensation as a retention signalBecause median salary and AI risk correlate at -0.24 across records and -0.81 across job titles, review pay bands for high-risk but business-critical roles rather than applying uniform salary assumptions.
Shift hiring toward resilient demand poolsExpand hiring pipelines in roles with the strongest openings growth, led by Product Manager (+546,788 openings from 2015 to 2035), while scrutinizing roles with contracting demand such as DevOps Engineer (-437,347).
Target geography-aware workforce planningCountry-level risk ranges from 0.39 in UK to 0.40 in India; use localized automation and redeployment strategies instead of a single global playbook.

Execution priorities

  • 0–6 months: Build a role-by-role AI exposure register for the top-risk roles and align it to business-critical workflows.
  • 6–18 months: Launch targeted reskilling academies for the fastest-growing skills and track migration into higher-survival role-skill combinations.
  • 18+ months: Rebalance workforce plans toward roles and geographies where openings growth and survival indicators remain strongest through 2035.
Methodology: Analysis uses the columns documented in /app/benchmark/source_brief.md: year, job title, country, experience level, education level, salary, AI risk score, primary skill, skill demand score, job openings, job survival class, salary bucket, and AI risk category. Future years are projections. No external data or fabricated figures are used. Generated as a self-contained HTML report with embedded images.
